title: Letter 4 — How a Living Faith Is Kindled in the Heart
attribution_note: Letter 4 of 46 in the collection Letters Sent — see Letter 1 for provenance. Part of the four-letter treatise On Faith (Letters 2–5); see Letter 2's note.

pairs.en: You ask: what must be done in order to have a living faith?

I answer. Christ says to us: *“Ask, and it shall be given you; seek, and ye shall find; knock, and it shall be opened unto you.”* [Matthew 7:7] We must ask, and seek, and knock. We must pray, and labour, and consider the means by which this faith, with God's help, is kindled in the heart. Do, then, as follows:

1) Remember often the incarnation of the Son of God, and meditate upon it. For He is *“the author and finisher”* of faith. [Hebrews 12:2] Remember and consider how the great God, the Maker of heaven and earth, came into the world for your sake; how He was born in the flesh of a Virgin, and how God was pleased to become man, and the Son of God to be called and to be the Son of man; how He lived on earth like one of the poor, and dwelt among sinners, and how for the sake of sinners He walked, laboured, hungered and thirsted; how God, whom the angels honour, endured blasphemy and reproach from sinners, and was persecuted.

Remember that night in which He grieved, was sorrowful, was seized with dread, and wept, kneeling before His Heavenly Father, and was strengthened by an angel appearing to Him from heaven: *“and His sweat was as it were great drops of blood falling down to the ground.”* [Luke 22:44] Remember the night in which He was sold and betrayed by His own disciple into the hands of lawless men, and, bound, was led away to the council, and the Judge of all was judged, and was struck on the face, and mocked, and wounded, and spat upon, and forsaken by all. Remember that morning in which He was led by His own lawless people to Pilate, and the Teacher of truth was slandered before him as a corrupter, and was sent by him to Herod, and reproached, mocked and derided.

Remember that time in which the multitudes cried out against Him to Pilate: *“Away with Him, away with Him, crucify Him!”* [John 19:15] — and preferred to Him Barabbas, a robber, an evildoer and a murderer; that time when He *“gave”* His *“back to the smiters,”* and His cheeks *“to them that plucked off the hair”* [Isaiah 50:6]; when the soldiers *“put on Him a scarlet robe,”* and crowned Him with thorns, and spat upon Him, and struck Him with a reed, and, as if He were a king, greeted Him with mockery: *“Hail, King of the Jews!”* [Matthew 27:28, 29] — when, amid the throng of a great multitude, He was led to His crucifixion as one condemned, and was nailed naked to the cross, and was hanged as an evildoer between two robbers, and was mocked by those passing by, and, when He thirsted, tasted the vinegar the soldiers brought to His lips.

Remember that time in which our God and Lord suffered for us, His unworthy servants, and hold firmly that He drank this cup of suffering for the sake of all, and for your sake too, thus working out our salvation; and consider that He is no mere man, but the Son of God and God, King and King's Son; and think that you deserve nothing but eternal torment without Him, as an enemy and apostate from God — but He, pitying you, as He pities all, and desiring to bring you and all men into God's mercy, and to reconcile you, and so to save you, took no thought for Himself, and gave Himself over to suffering and death, that so — that is, by His suffering and death — He might deliver you from eternal suffering and death, and bring you into eternal blessedness. Be firmly assured, then, that He is your Redeemer, Deliverer, Saviour, Helper, Defender, hope, and eternal life, and every blessedness, and that apart from Him and without Him you have no hope and no salvation at all.

When you have considered all this, and are assured of it, a living faith in Him will most certainly be kindled in your heart by the grace of the Holy Spirit — a faith that works by love, by thanksgiving, by patience and the other virtues, and shows itself alive. When such a faith is kindled in your heart, you will most certainly feel faith also in His Heavenly Father. For, having learned that the Son of God came to save you and suffered for you, you will at once learn also the love of the Heavenly Father toward you, who for your sake did not spare His own Son, but gave Him up to suffering and death. For it was by the good pleasure of the Heavenly Father, and by His own will, that Jesus the Son of God suffered for us. And from this there will follow an unshaken hope of eternal life and blessedness, and of the fulfilment of all God's merciful promises: *“He that spared not His own Son, but delivered Him up for us all, how shall He not with Him also freely give us all things?”* [Romans 8:32] Since God has done so great and wondrous a deed — that for our sake He was pleased that His own Son should become flesh and suffer — how shall He not fulfil everything He has promised us for His sake? *“The Lord is faithful in all His words”* [Psalm 144:13]; *“His mercy toward us is unshaken, and the truth of the Lord endureth for ever.”* [Psalm 116:2]

sections.heading: Live as one who walks before God

pairs.en: 2) Holy Scripture sets before us that God is everywhere, and sees everything, and looks upon all our deeds, thoughts, undertakings and intentions, and understands them, and hears every word. Believe, then, that He is present with you too, and that you do, think, undertake, devise and speak everything before Him, and that He knows every deed, thought and word of yours far better than you do yourself — and believe this firmly, without doubt. Then, without doubt, you will feel a quickening in your soul, and fear, and trembling, reverence, and caution in your deeds and thoughts; and you will walk before Him as subjects walk before their king, as children before their father, and as servants before their master — guarding against all that is evil, and striving to do all that is good. Look upon Him with the eye of mind and faith, as you look upon a king, or a master, or your father, when you are in their presence — as the prophet said of himself: *“I have set the Lord always before me: because He is at my right hand, I shall not be moved.”* [Psalm 15:8] He is *“not far from every one of us,”* though we do not see Him. [Acts 17:27] Be firmly assured of this, and then you will most certainly feel everything else within yourself: then will be born in you the spirit of the fear of God, of reverence, of hope, of prayer, and the rest.

3) When you pray, think without doubt that you are standing before God, and falling down before Him, and asking Him for what you need, and speaking with Him as a subject stands before his king and entreats him — and then there will be born in you a spirit of humility, of fear, and of hope. For as great as God is, so immeasurably good and true is He also. The thought of His greatness will make you afraid and humble you; but the thought of His goodness and truth will encourage you, and confirm you in the hope that He has promised to hear us, *“all them that call upon Him in truth.”* [Psalm 144:18–19]

sections.heading: Honor the Word, and trust His care for you

pairs.en: 4) Be firmly assured concerning Holy Scripture, that it is the true Word of God, the word of God's own mouth; the mouth of the Lord has spoken it, and He speaks in His Scripture to you, as to all men. Then reverence and zeal for the honouring and keeping of the Word of God will follow in your heart. Then, with the prophet, you will cry out to God from your heart: *“The law of Thy mouth is better unto me than thousands of gold and silver.”* [Psalm 118:72] For if you honour a letter sent to you by an earthly king, or a word he has spoken, and strive to carry it out, how much more will you hold the word of the Heavenly King in great honour. For as far as God is removed from an earthly king, who is but a man, so much more honourable and precious is His holy word than any human word. If you honour God with the highest honour, which faith requires of you, you will honour His holy word above everything else too.

From this will follow zealous keeping of His holy commandments, and faith in His holy and merciful promises and revelations. God speaks to you, commands you, reveals to you, promises you His mercy, calls you to repentance and to eternal life, and the rest, in His Scripture. He is no respecter of persons, as man is: He has given His holy word equally to you, as to all, for the salvation of your soul.

5) Be assured in your heart that God cares for you, as He cares for all. His sun shines for you, He sends rain upon you, He gives you food, drink, clothing and a home. He guards your life and keeps it from the devil's snares, and does you every other kindness every day, every hour, every minute, so that a man cannot live even the smallest minute without His kindness. All this the all-good God does for you out of pure goodness and love for mankind. What can follow from this but love for Him, zealous thanksgiving, and the diligent doing of His will, without which there can be no love or thanksgiving? For if you love and thank a man who has done you some small kindness, how much more will you love and thank God, the Giver of all good things, from whom you have everything — your very being and your life. For conscience itself persuades you to this.

sections.heading: Wonder at the mystery of God made man

pairs.en: 6) Be assured, and confess not with your lips alone but believe with your heart, that Christ is God, one in essence with the Father and the Spirit, one of the Persons of the Holy Trinity, and that for your sake He came into the world, and was born of the holy Virgin, and lived on earth, and suffered, and died in the flesh, and rose from the dead, and so accomplished your eternal salvation. What can follow from this but wonder at the goodness of God, and heartfelt thanksgiving, and love for Him and for His Heavenly Father, by whose good pleasure the incarnation of His Son came to pass? Believe me, beloved, I speak the truth to you: as often as we consider this great deed with living faith, so often shall we be found in wonder and a kind of rapture. It is impossible to marvel enough at God's goodness toward us sinners, in everything, but especially in the work of our salvation. Truly *“the Lord hath done marvellous things”*! [Psalm 97:1] Search through all history, examine the whole of nature, and you will find no example worthy to be compared with the great and wonderful work of God's incarnation. The great and incomprehensible God, the Lord and eternal King, for the sake of His unworthy servant — and more than that, for the sake of His enemy — came into the world, and appeared in the flesh, and suffered, and died for his sake, that He might make him eternally blessed.

Blessed is God, who was so well pleased! Read attentively the apostolic epistles, especially those of holy Paul, and you will see how the apostles marvel at this great work of God and glorify His goodness. Christ our Lord Himself sets before us this goodness of God for our wonder: *“For God so loved the world, that He gave His only begotten Son, that whosoever believeth in Him should not perish, but have everlasting life.”* [John 3:16]

It is a great thing that God created the world out of nothing; but it is a still greater thing that He was pleased to become flesh for the sake of man, His apostate and enemy. Here the mind — not the mind of man only, but even the mind of angels — fails and grows dull in its reflection. A created mind cannot glorify this worthily, for it can only truly marvel at it. *“Blessed be the name of the Lord for ever and ever”*! [Daniel 2:20] Consider this often, and you will always be in wonder and heartfelt thanksgiving.

sections.heading: Prepare for the table, and for the judgment

pairs.en: 7) Be exactly assured and confirmed that the Body of Christ and His Blood are truly present in the most holy Eucharist — and this conviction will teach you with what fear, honour and reverence you must approach that great Mystery. Men go to a king's table with fear, and preparation, and reverence — and will you not tremble, drawing near to this divine table? Then you will not say much in your prayer, but will repeat only this: “Have mercy on me, O Lord; cleanse me, O Lord, lest I be burned up like dry hay by the fire.” For the Holy Things are given to the holy, as the priest proclaims at the Liturgy: “Holy Things for the holy.” And here you will marvel at the goodness of God, that the Body of Christ and His most holy Blood are given to us, frail and unworthy as we are, for spiritual food; and from your heart you will bless and thank Him for this great Mystery of His; and, keeping this in mind, you will conduct yourself more carefully in your life, and will not want to defile your conscience and your soul with sins, but will strive in every way to live as befits a Christian. This alone will turn you away from every sin, and stir you up to every good work.

8) Believe truly that there will be a universal judgment of Christ, and that you, with all men, will stand at that judgment before God the Judge, and give account for all your evil deeds, words and thoughts. What can follow from this but fear of this judgment, true repentance, contrition, heartfelt sighing, and prayer — that you may not be condemned at that judgment, and may not hear that dreadful sentence from the Judge: *“Depart from Me, ye cursed, into everlasting fire”*! [Matthew 25:41]

Human judgment is dreadful to men, and they prepare themselves for it in every way, so as not to be put to shame — shall the judgment of God not be dreadful to you, at which there will be no respect of persons, and every deed, word and thought of yours will be as open before Him then as it is now, unless you are cleansed by repentance? *“I will rebuke thee, and set thy sins in order before thine eyes,”* says God through the Psalmist. [Psalm 49:21] Truly He will rebuke every sinner! Truly He will set his sins before his face! Truly then those will wish to hide in caves and among rocks who now are not content with a few small comforts, but are forever devising and building new ones. Then they will learn that they are nothing — though here they count themselves as something great.

Be assured, then, about that judgment, and you will be other than you were before, and are now. A true reflection upon it changes a man, and makes him spiritual instead of carnal. A man will no longer wish to provoke his conscience by any sin, but will turn away from every sin; he will be bound by its fear as by a rope, and made immovable toward every evil. And, to add fear to fear, the day of judgment will come unexpectedly, as a thief in the night. It is already near, and nearer today than it was yesterday, and when we least expect it, the *“voice of the Bridegroom”* will be heard. Stand watch, then, and wait. Blessed is he who watches! He *“shall be caught up in the clouds”* with those who have died in Christ and are then risen, *“to meet the Lord in the air.”* [1 Thessalonians 4:17]

9) Believe without doubt, and firmly, that there will be eternal torment for sinners who do not truly repent and do not have living faith in Christ in their hearts. Be confirmed in this, and when you see fire in an oven, look with the eye of your mind on the eternal fire, and then you will feel everything new in your heart. Then true repentance, sighing and prayer will be born within you. Then you will not say much, but will always attend to yourself, and often fall down before God in humility, and sigh, and say from the depths of your heart: “Lord, have mercy; Lord, spare me; Lord, deliver me, for Thy name's sake!” Then all worldly comfort, joy and sweetness will vanish from your heart, and you will turn away, as from a deadly poison, from every sin that leads to that disaster. Believe me, I tell you the truth: this will be on your mind, and this will be your care and concern — how to be delivered from that disaster from which Christ alone delivers us, but delivers those who listen to Him and obey Him, not those who resist Him. If you strive to flee from temporal sorrow, grief, sickness, prison, torment, exile and other misfortune, will you not strive still more to flee from an eternal and unending misfortune? Everything temporal is nothing against the eternal, because the temporal ends easily, but the eternal is grievous and never ends.
O eternal fire, dreadful even to demons! Deliver us from it, O most merciful Christ. Let Thy mercy toward us, O Lord, be as great as Thy majesty!

10) Be exactly assured that you are a stranger and a pilgrim in this world, and held in captivity, and that your fatherland and your home are not here, but in the heavens, and there your inheritance, your treasure, your glory and honour are prepared by God. You were created, and renewed by holy Baptism, as all men are, not for this world, not for honour, riches, glory and the other visible goods, but for the eternal goods which *“eye hath not seen, nor ear heard, neither have entered into the heart of man, the things which God hath prepared for them that love Him.”* [1 Corinthians 2:9] You are called to eternal life [1 Timothy 6:12], invited to the great supper [Luke 14:16–23], where the righteous *“shall hunger no more, neither thirst any more; neither shall the sun light on them, nor any heat: for the Lamb, which is in the midst of the throne, shall feed them, and shall lead them unto living fountains of waters: and God shall wipe away all tears from their eyes”* [Revelation 7:16–17] — where *“they shall receive the royal dignity and the crown of beauty at the hand of the Lord”* [Wisdom 5:16], where *“the righteous shall shine forth as the sun”* [Matthew 13:43], where the servants of the Lord shall eat and drink and be glad [Isaiah 65:13–14], where they shall see God *“face to face”* [1 Corinthians 13:12], shall *“see Him as He is”* [1 John 3:2], and the rest.

Be firmly assured that eternal life and eternal glory will most certainly be given, according to God's promise, to those who are faithful in Christ. What can follow from this in you but a ceaseless desire to obtain these eternal goods? Believe me, I tell you the truth: this will be in your mind, your thought and your heart; there all your attention will be, and there you will send your sighing and desire, according to Christ's word: *“Where”* your *“treasure”* is, *“there will”* your *“heart be also.”* [Matthew 6:21; Luke 12:34]

So too with everything else that the holy Word of God declares — you must be firmly assured of it, and from this, with God's help, a living faith will be born in your heart. *“For the word of God is quick, and powerful, and sharper than any twoedged sword, piercing even to the dividing asunder of soul and spirit, and of the joints and marrow, and is a discerner of the thoughts and intents of the heart.”* [Hebrews 4:12] And since the Word of God is alive, it also produces a living fruit: it makes a man spiritually alive, by the power of the Holy Spirit, from whom it came forth for our salvation and renewal.

Yet know for certain that everything in us that God Himself does not produce is dead and worthless. Therefore we must pray earnestly, and ask God, that He Himself would work in us and make us spiritually alive. This is why we are commanded to “ask, and seek, and knock,” as I wrote to you at the beginning.
Be saved.
